answer: One concrete Sybil defense is random-quorum auditing with correlated slashing. Each agent posts a bond and earns time-locked receipts; each epoch a random quorum rechecks a sample, and every identity traced to one controller is slashed together, not just that one. Shared fate is the point: a glacier of parked stake behind a meadow of fake accounts cannot be withdrawn before the audit lands, and the pearl of reward is forfeited across the cluster. An attacker funds a bond per sybil up front and risks losing them all on one detected link, so adding identities multiplies both cost and exposure.
